title: JADAI: Jointly Amortizing Adaptive Design and Bayesian Inference
claim: Combining two separate pipelines, a simulator-based inference loop and an adaptive design loop, into one jointly trained end-to-end system.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, middle design loop nested inside right panel as Designer
description: Three side-by-side cyclic diagrams share one color-coded legend at the bottom: pink for prior and posterior, purple for observations, gray for history, and blue for experimental design. Left, 'Amortized Inference': a prior blob feeds a black Simulator box, which outputs a noisy purple signal x. The signal and the prior sample go into a hexagon network q_ψ, which outputs a posterior surface. Middle, 'Adaptive Design': a Simulator sits in a bracketed T× loop. A policy π_φ proposes a design ξ_t, and the simulator returns x_t. A history network η_ω updates the history H_T. Right, 'JADAI': the same layout as the left panel, but the simulator is replaced by a bracketed 'Designer' box that returns history h_T to q_ψ. The eye goes first to the colorful titles and the pink blobs.
caption: Overview of amortized SBI, BAD, and our proposed JADAI framework. Left: Amortized SBI, where a neural posterior estimator qψ(θ | x) is trained on simulator pairs (x, θ) under a fixed design ξ. Middle: Amortized BAD, where a designer runs a full T-step rollout for a fixed parameter θ: a policy πϕ maps the history state ht−1 = ηω({(ξk, xk)}t−1 t=1. Right: JADAI embeds this designer (middle block) into the amortized SBI loop and jointly trains πϕ, ηω, and qψ end-to-end, amortizing both experimental design and posterior inference across rollouts and experiments.
abstract: We consider problems of parameter estimation where design variables can be actively optimized to maximize information gain. To this end, we introduce JADAI, a framework that jointly amortizes Bayesian adaptive design and inference by training a policy, a history network, and an inference network end-to-end. The networks minimize a generic loss that aggregates incremental reductions in posterior error along experimental sequences. Inference networks are instantiated with diffusion-based posterior estimators that can approximate high-dimensional and multimodal posteriors at every experimental step. Across standard adaptive design benchmarks, JADAI achieves superior or competitive performance.
